sources.title: Richard F. Bass, Real Analysis for Graduate Students, Version 5.0
sources.locator: Contents p. v; Section 9.1, printed pp. 77-79, from the heading "Comparison with the Lebesgue integral" through Theorem 9.1 and Examples 9.2-9.3; Section 9.2, printed pp. 79-81, Exercises 9.2, 9.4, 9.6, and 9.7

contents.name: Theorem 9.1, a bounded real-valued function on [a,b] is Riemann integrable iff its discontinuity set has Lebesgue measure 0, and in that case the Riemann and Lebesgue integrals agree
Example 9.2, the Dirichlet indicator on [0,1] is not Riemann integrable
Example 9.3, Thomae's function is Riemann integrable because its discontinuity set is countable
Exercise 9.2, find a continuous function on (0,1] whose improper Riemann integral exists although it is not Lebesgue integrable
Exercise 9.4, if a Lebesgue integrable function has an improper Riemann limit then the two values agree
Exercise 9.6, the upper Darboux envelope agrees almost everywhere with the bounded measurable function
Exercise 9.7, a bounded measurable function with a positive-measure discontinuity set is not Riemann integrable

sources.title: Richard L. Wheeden and Antoni Zygmund, Measure and Integral: An Introduction to Real Analysis
sources.locator: Section 5, from the heading "Riemann and Lebesgue Integrals" through Theorems (5.52) and (5.53); Section 10, Corollary (10.32); Section 11.3, Theorem (11.11)

contents.name: (5.52) Theorem, every bounded Riemann integrable function is Lebesgue integrable with the same value
(5.53) Theorem, a nonnegative improper Riemann integral on a finite interval is Lebesgue integrable with the same value
(11.11) Theorem, the Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral extends the Riemann-Stieltjes integral

contents.name: Example 2.22, a measurable subset of the Cantor set that is not Borel measurable

canonical.name: A bounded Riemann integrable function admits Borel Darboux envelopes with zero integral gap
A bounded Riemann integrable function on a closed bounded interval is Lebesgue measurable and has the same integral
A Riemann integrable function on a closed bounded interval is almost everywhere equal to a Borel function
Arzela's bounded convergence theorem for Riemann integrals
A nonnegative improper Riemann integral on a half-line agrees with the Lebesgue integral
For a continuous integrand, the Riemann-Stieltjes and Lebesgue-Stieltjes integrals agree
The indicator of the rationals in [0,1] is Lebesgue integrable with integral 0 and not Riemann integrable
FALSE: every Riemann integrable function on a closed bounded interval is Borel measurable
An open dense set of measure less than 1 is the monotone L1-limit of Riemann integrable indicators, but its indicator is not Riemann integrable
The sine integral is improperly Riemann integrable and not Lebesgue integrable
The indicator of a fat Cantor set is upper semicontinuous and equal almost everywhere to no Riemann integrable function
A null set can fail to be the discontinuity set of any function
